newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar holds firmness, crosses prevail.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar holds firmness, crosses prevail.

text.p: Crossed trades accounted for the bulk of white sugar futures volume on Wednesday morning as the market languished ahead of the open of New York and the remaining time before the May raws expiry.
The nearby August/October spread remained at around $6.20, roughly the same as on Tuesday, with some broker crossing accounted for some 100 lots of the volume.
"Bits and pieces have traded but it's basically still quite firm. The whites are just sitting here and waiting," said one trader.
Ranges were tight on the three contracts traded and at 1115 GMT spot August was up 60 cents at $311.50. October was up 70 cents at $305.60 and volume reached a scant 309 lots.
Traders also noted October crossing from one leading commission house and light Paris-based selling as pre-hedging against the weekly EU tender for export licences.
Most attention was concentrated on New York, where fund players have increased their long July positions and continued to bale out of May before expiry on April 30.

London traders cited July stops at 11.18 cents/lb. Physical deliveries are expected to be dominated by central American origins, while north Brazil is still thought to be holding a substantial amount of raws.

In other news, around 140,000 tonnes of raws are held up at Novorossisk because of bad weather and a lack of rail wagons needed to transport the sugar inland. Some raws are also reported to be arriving via Riga.
In Paris 252 lots of May were posted on the board. The position was unchanged at $311.00.
